## The Print

Apple's FY2025 revenue rose 6.4% to $416.2B, with net income up 19.5% to $112.0B and diluted EPS up 22.7% to $7.46.

Revenue growth accelerated from 2.0% in FY2024 to 6.4% in FY2025, with Services surpassing $100B for the first time and iPhone returning to growth.

- Total net sales increased 6.4% year over year to $416.2B, driven by growth in Services and iPhone.
- Net income increased 19.5% to $112.0B, reflecting a lower effective tax rate and higher operating income.
- Diluted EPS increased 22.7% to $7.46, aided by a 2.6% reduction in weighted-average diluted shares outstanding.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $416.2B | $391.0B | +6.5% | Growth was driven by higher net sales of iPhone and Services, partially offset by a decline in Wearables, Home and Accessories. |
| Operating income | $133.1B | $123.2B | +8.0% | Operating income increased due to higher total net sales and improved gross margin, partially offset by higher operating expenses. |
| Operating margin | 32.0% | 31.5% | +0.5 ppts | Operating margin expanded as gross margin improvement outpaced the increase in operating expenses as a percentage of revenue. |
| Diluted EPS | $7.46 | $6.08 | +22.7% | Diluted EPS growth exceeded net income growth due to a reduction in weighted-average diluted shares outstanding from share repurchases. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net income of $112.0B includes a $10.7B year-over-year decrease in the provision for income taxes related to the State Aid Decision, which was a one-time charge in FY2024. Excluding this item, the effective tax rate would have been higher, and net income growth would have been lower. Operating income growth of 8.0% was driven by core operations, with no material one-time items disclosed.

Operating cash flow was 1.0x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $98.8B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $15.4B (prior $15.2B), share repurchases $90.7B (prior $94.9B); capital expenditures $12.7B (prior $9.4B).

Apple continued its aggressive capital return program, repurchasing $89.3B of common stock and paying $15.4B in dividends. The company also announced a new $100B share repurchase program in May 2025 and raised its quarterly dividend by 4% to $0.26 per share. Capital expenditures increased 34.6% to $12.7B, reflecting investments in manufacturing and data center infrastructure. The allocation is funded entirely by operating cash flow, which exceeded capital returns.

Return on equity was 151.9% (prior 164.6%); return on assets 31.2% (prior 25.7%).

- In May 2025, the Company announced a new share repurchase program of up to $100 billion and raised its quarterly dividend from $0.25 to $0.26 per share beginning in May 2025.

## Forward Signals

The Company does not provide quantitative guidance. Management noted that gross margins will be subject to volatility and downward pressure due to factors discussed in Risk Factors.

**Known trends**
- Tariffs and other trade measures announced in 2025 could materially adversely affect the Company's business, results of operations, and financial condition.
- The Company expects its effective tax rate to be impacted by changes in unrecognized tax benefits and foreign earnings mix.

> "The Company believes, in general, gross margins will be subject to volatility and downward pressure." — Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Tariffs and other trade measures could increase costs, disrupt supply chain, and reduce demand for products. | Beginning in the second quarter of 2025, new tariffs were announced on imports to the U.S. ("U.S. Tariffs"), including additional tariffs on imports from China, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam and the European Union ("EU"), among others. |
| 2 | Dependence on single or limited sources for critical components exposes the company to supply shortages and price increases. | Because the Company currently obtains certain components from single or limited sources, the Company is subject to significant supply and pricing risks. |
| 3 | Intense competition in global markets could pressure margins and market share. | The Company's products and services are offered in highly competitive global markets. These markets are characterized by aggressive price competition, downward pressure on gross margins, continual improvement in product performance, and price sensitivity on the part of consumers and businesses. |
| 4 | Legal proceedings and government investigations, including patent claims and regulatory actions, could result in significant costs and business restrictions. | The Company has faced and continues to face a significant number of patent claims relating to its standards-enabled products, and new claims may arise in the future. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Americas | $178.4B | $72.5B | +6.8% | 43% of segment revenue, 41% operating margin — Net sales increased primarily due to higher net sales of iPhone and Services, with unfavorable foreign currency impact. |
| Europe | $111.0B | $47.7B | +9.6% | 27% of segment revenue, 43% operating margin — Net sales increased primarily due to higher net sales of Services, iPhone and Mac. |
| Greater China | $64.4B | $26.9B | -3.8% | 15% of segment revenue, 42% operating margin — Net sales decreased primarily due to lower net sales of iPhone, partially offset by higher net sales of Mac. |
| Rest of Asia Pacific | $33.7B | $14.6B | +9.9% | 8% of segment revenue, 43% operating margin — Net sales increased primarily due to higher net sales of iPhone, Services and Mac. |
| Japan | $28.7B | $14.0B | +14.6% | 7% of segment revenue, 49% operating margin — Net sales increased primarily due to higher net sales of iPhone, Services and iPad. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt (term debt plus commercial paper) was $98.7B, while cash and marketable securities totaled $132.4B, resulting in a net cash position of $33.7B. Shareholders' equity was $73.7B, giving a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.34x.

Liquidity: Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $132.4B as of September 27, 2025. Management believes this, along with operating cash flow and access to debt markets, is sufficient to meet cash requirements and capital return program over the next 12 months and beyond.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $111.5B, investing $15.2B, financing $-120.7B.

Working capital: Current assets $148.0B vs. current liabilities $165.6B (current ratio 0.89x). A year earlier: $153.0B vs. $176.4B (0.87x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- As of September 27, 2025, the Company had $12.4B of term debt payable within 12 months.
- The Company had $8.0B of commercial paper outstanding, payable within 12 months.

## Notable Footnotes

| Item | Impact |
| --- | --- |
| European Commission State Aid Decision | In FY2024, the Company recorded a one-time income tax charge of $10.2B net related to the ECJ's confirmation of the 2016 State Aid Decision. This charge was absent in FY2025, contributing to the lower effective tax rate. |
| Segment Reporting Adoption | The Company adopted ASU 2023-07, which requires disclosure of segment expenses significant to the CODM. This resulted in additional segment disclosures, including operating income by segment. |

Revenue, net income, and EPS all more than doubled year-over-year, with gross margin expanding significantly due to the non-recurrence of a prior-year inventory charge.

- Revenue increased 85% YoY to $81.6B, driven by Data Center demand for Blackwell 300 products and networking solutions.
- Net income rose 211% YoY to $58.3B, and diluted EPS increased 214% YoY to $2.39.
- Gross margin expanded 14.4 percentage points YoY to 74.9%, primarily due to the absence of a prior-year $4.5B H20 inventory charge.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |

| Diluted EPS | $2.39 | $0.76 | +214.5% | EPS growth outpaced net income growth due to a lower diluted share count from share repurchases. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net income of $58.3B includes $15.9B of other income, primarily $13.4B unrealized gains on publicly-held equity securities and $2.6B unrealized gains on non-marketable equity securities. Excluding these non-operating gains, operating income was $53.5B, up 147% YoY.

- Total revenue decreased $2.86B to $94.83B, driven by a 9% decline in automotive sales revenue to $65.82B, partially offset by a 27% increase in energy generation and storage revenue to $12.77B.
- Net income attributable to common stockholders fell to $3.79B from $7.09B, while diluted EPS declined to $1.08 from $2.04.

## The Print

Tesla's 2025 revenue declined 2.9% to $94.8B while net income fell 46.5% to $3.8B, driven by lower automotive deliveries and regulatory credit revenue, partially offset by growth in energy storage.

Revenue and profitability declined year-over-year as automotive sales and regulatory credits fell, while energy storage and services grew, and operating expenses rose sharply on AI-related R&D.

- Total revenue decreased $2.86B to $94.83B, with automotive revenue down 10% and energy generation and storage up 27%.
- Net income attributable to common stockholders fell to $3.79B from $7.09B, and diluted EPS declined to $1.08 from $2.04.
- Operating cash flow remained strong at $14.75B, and free cash flow improved to $6.22B from $3.58B due to lower capital expenditures.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $94.83B | $97.69B | −2.9% | Decrease driven by lower automotive sales volume and average selling price, partially offset by growth in energy generation and storage and services. |
| Operating income | $4.36B | $7.08B | −38.4% | Decline due to lower gross profit and higher operating expenses, particularly R&D and SG&A. |
| Operating margin | 4.6% | 7.2% | −2.6 ppts | Margin compression from lower automotive gross margin and increased R&D spending as a percentage of revenue. |
| Diluted EPS | $1.08 | $2.04 | −47.1% | Lower net income attributable to common stockholders, partially offset by a slight increase in diluted weighted average shares. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net income includes $494M in restructuring and other charges (2025) and $684M (2024), primarily from employee terminations and asset impairments. Excluding these, operating results still declined due to lower automotive gross profit and higher R&D. Digital asset mark-to-market losses of $68M in 2025 vs. gains of $589M in 2024 also impacted other income.

Operating cash flow was 3.9x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $6.2B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital expenditures $8.5B (prior $11.3B).

Capital expenditures decreased 24.8% to $8.53B, but management expects capex to exceed $20B in 2026, driven by AI infrastructure and manufacturing expansion. The company continues to prioritize investments in autonomy, robotics, and energy storage over shareholder returns, with no dividends or buybacks disclosed.

Return on equity was 4.6% (prior 9.7%); return on assets 2.8% (prior 5.8%).

## Forward Signals

Management expects capital expenditures to exceed $20 billion in 2026, driven by AI initiatives, manufacturing expansion, and growth in company-operated AI-enabled assets. No specific revenue or earnings guidance was provided.

**Known trends**
- Rapidly evolving trade and fiscal policy, including tariffs, could adversely impact supply chain costs and demand.
- The OBBBA removal of EV tax credits may reduce consumer demand for electric vehicles.
- Energy storage deployments can vary quarter to quarter based on project milestones and logistics.

**Subsequent events**
- In January 2026, the Company entered into an agreement to make a minority equity investment in xAI.

> "We currently expect our capital expenditures to be in excess of $20 billion in 2026, driven by our AI initiatives, including investments in compute infrastructure and data centers, the expansion and ramp of our manufacturing and R&D production lines and facilities, and growth in our fleet of company-operated AI-enabled assets and our retail, service and charging footprint." — Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Dependence on Elon Musk, who does not devote full time to Tesla and holds management positions at other companies. | We are highly dependent on the services of Elon Musk, Technoking of Tesla and our Chief Executive Officer. Although Mr. Musk spends significant time with Tesla and is highly active in our management, he does not devote his full time and attention to Tesla. |
| 2 | Supply chain disruptions and tariffs could increase costs and limit component availability, particularly for battery cells and AI-related hardware. | U.S. trade policy alterations in 2025, including heightened import tariffs and subsequent retaliatory measures, have impacted our supply chain costs, and may impact the availability of certain technologies or components. |
| 3 | Product liability and regulatory scrutiny related to autonomous driving and vehicle safety could result in significant costs and reputational harm. | We have experienced, and we expect to continue to face, claims and regulatory scrutiny arising from or related to misuse or claimed failures or alleged misrepresentations of the technologies that we are pioneering. |
| 4 | Competition in electric vehicles and autonomous ride-hailing is intensifying, with many established and new entrants. | A significant and growing number of established and new automobile manufacturers, as well as other companies, have entered, or are reported to have plans to enter, the market for electric and other alternative fuel vehicles, including hybrid, plug-in hybrid and fully electric vehicles, as well as the market for self-driving technology and services. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Automotive segment | $82.1B |  | -6.3% | 87% of segment revenue — Automotive sales revenue decreased 9% due to lower cash deliveries and lower average selling price from sales mix and higher customer incentives. Regulatory credits fell 28% due to OBBBA restrictions. |
| Energy generation and storage segment | $12.8B |  | +26.6% | 13% of segment revenue — Revenue increased 27% driven by higher Megapack and Powerwall deployments, partially offset by lower Megapack average selling price. Gross margin improved to 29.8% from 26.2%. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt (including finance leases) was $8.18B, with $1.58B current. Cash and investments totaled $44.06B, resulting in a net cash position of approximately $35.9B. Debt-to-equity ratio was 0.10.

Liquidity: Cash and cash equivalents of $16.51B plus short-term investments of $27.55B, and $6.43B of unused committed credit. Management believes current sources provide adequate liquidity for at least the next 12 months.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $14.7B, investing $-15.5B, financing $1.1B.

- Outstanding indebtedness of $8.18B, of which $1.58B is current.

## The Print

Amazon's 2025 revenue increased 12% to $716.9B, with net income of $77.7B and diluted EPS of $7.17.

Revenue growth accelerated to 12% from 11% in 2024, while net income rose 31% on higher operating income and a $15.2B gain from Anthropic-related investments.

- Revenue increased 12% YoY to $716.9B, driven by AWS growth of 20%.
- Net income increased 31% YoY to $77.7B, with diluted EPS of $7.17.
- Operating cash flow increased 20% to $139.5B, but free cash flow fell to $11.2B due to a 65% increase in capital expenditures.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $716.9B | $638.0B | +12.4% | Sales increased 12% in 2025, compared to the prior year. Changes in foreign exchange rates increased net sales by $4.4 billion in 2025. |
| Operating income | $80.0B | $68.6B | +16.6% | Operating income was $68.6 billion and $80.0 billion for 2024 and 2025. Operating income for 2025 includes charges of $2.5 billion we recorded in Q3 2025 related to the settlement of a lawsuit with the FTC and $2.7 billion, of which $1.8 billion was recorded in Q3 2025, of estimated severance costs primarily related to planned role eliminations. |
| Operating margin | 11.2% | 10.8% | +0.4 ppts | Operating margin expanded 0.4 percentage points to 11.2%, as revenue growth outpaced operating expense growth. |
| Diluted EPS | $7.17 | $5.53 | +29.7% | Diluted EPS increased 29.7% to $7.17, driven by higher net income and a modest increase in weighted-average diluted shares. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net income of $77.7B includes a $15.2B gain in other income (expense), net, primarily from upward adjustments and reclassification gains related to Anthropic investments. Excluding this non-operating gain, pre-tax operating income was $80.0B, up 16.6% YoY. Operating income itself included $2.5B FTC settlement charge, $2.7B severance costs, and $1.3B asset impairments, which partially offset underlying growth.

Operating cash flow was 1.8x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $7.7B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital expenditures $131.8B (prior $83.0B).

Capital allocation shifted heavily toward growth capex, with cash capital expenditures rising 65% to $128.3B, primarily for AWS infrastructure. The company issued $15.7B in long-term debt and generated positive financing cash flow of $9.7B, while free cash flow fell to $11.2B from $38.2B. No dividends or share repurchases were reported.

Return on equity was 18.9% (prior 20.7%); return on assets 9.5% (prior 9.5%).

## Forward Signals

First quarter 2026 net sales are expected to be between $173.5 billion and $178.5 billion, or to grow between 11% and 15% compared with first quarter 2025. Operating income is expected to be between $16.5 billion and $21.5 billion, compared with $18.4 billion in first quarter 2025.

**Known trends**
- Management expects spending in technology and infrastructure to increase over time, including to support artificial intelligence and machine learning initiatives.
- The company anticipates continued investment in AWS infrastructure and fulfillment network capacity, with capital expenditures expected to increase in 2026.

**Subsequent events**
- Subsequent to December 31, 2025, an additional portion of Amazon's convertible notes in Anthropic was converted to nonvoting preferred stock, resulting in an expected gain of approximately $3 billion in Q1 2026, plus an upward adjustment of approximately $12 billion to the nonvoting preferred stock.

> "We expect spending in technology and infrastructure will increase over time, which can negatively impact short-term free cash flow, as we add infrastructure and employees, including to support our artificial intelligence and machine learning initiatives, to support long-term growth." — Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Intense competition across all business segments, including e-commerce, cloud services, and advertising, could reduce sales and profits. | Our businesses are rapidly evolving and intensely competitive, and we have many competitors across geographies, including cross-border competition, and in different industries, including physical, e-commerce, and omnichannel retail, e-commerce services, web and infrastructure computing services, electronic devices, digital content, advertising, grocery, healthcare, communications, and transportation and logistics services. |
| 2 | International operations expose Amazon to regulatory, economic, and geopolitical risks, particularly in China and India, where local laws may restrict foreign ownership and operations. | The People’s Republic of China (“PRC”) and India regulate Amazon’s and its affiliates’ businesses and operations in country through regulations and license requirements that may restrict (i) foreign investment in and operation of the internet, IT infrastructure, data centers, retail, delivery, and other sectors, (ii) internet content, and (iii) the sale of media and other products and services. |
| 3 | Dependence on a limited number of suppliers for semiconductor products, including GPUs for AI infrastructure, could disrupt operations if supply is constrained. | For example, we rely on a limited group of suppliers for semiconductor products, including products related to artificial intelligence infrastructure such as graphics processing units. Constraints on the availability of these products could adversely affect our ability to develop and operate artificial intelligence technologies, products, or services. |
| 4 | Foreign exchange rate fluctuations can materially impact reported results and intercompany balances, with significant gains or losses on remeasurement. | The results of operations of, and certain of our intercompany balances associated with, our international stores and product and service offerings are exposed to foreign exchange rate fluctuations. Due to these fluctuations, operating results may differ materially from expectations, and we may record significant gains or losses on the remeasurement of intercompany balances. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |

## The Print

ExxonMobil's 2025 revenue declined 5.0% to $332.2B, with net income attributable to ExxonMobil of $28.8B and diluted EPS of $6.70.

Revenue and earnings declined year-over-year primarily due to lower crude oil realizations, partially offset by record production volumes and structural cost savings.

- Revenue decreased 5.0% YoY to $332.2B, driven by lower crude prices and divestments.
- Net income attributable to ExxonMobil fell 14.4% to $28.8B, with diluted EPS down 14.5% to $6.70.
- Upstream production reached a 40-year high of 4.7 million oil-equivalent barrels per day, up 9.3% YoY.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $332.2B | $349.6B | −5.0% | Lower crude oil realizations and divestments drove the decline, partially offset by higher production volumes. |
| Operating income | $41.3B | $48.9B | −15.5% | Lower upstream realizations and higher depreciation from the Tengiz expansion reduced operating income. |
| Operating margin | 12.4% | 14.0% | −1.6 ppts | Margin compression reflects lower commodity prices and higher depreciation, partially offset by structural cost savings. |
| Diluted EPS | $6.70 | $7.84 | −14.5% | EPS declined in line with net income, with share repurchases partially offsetting the earnings decline. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net income included $0.9B of identified items in Upstream (mainly asset impairments) and a $0.5B gain in Energy Products (mainly asset sales). Excluding identified items, Upstream earnings were $22.2B and Energy Products earnings were $6.9B.

Operating cash flow was 1.8x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $23.6B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $17.2B (prior $16.7B), share repurchases $20.3B (prior $19.6B); capital expenditures $28.4B (prior $24.3B).

ExxonMobil continued to prioritize shareholder returns, with dividends and buybacks exceeding free cash flow, funded by cash on hand and debt issuance. Capital expenditures increased 16.7% to $28.4B, focused on advantaged Upstream projects and lower-emission investments.

Return on equity was 11.1% (prior 12.8%); return on assets 6.4% (prior 7.4%).

- Completed the divestment of Esso Société Anonyme Française SA and ExxonMobil Chemical France SAS in November 2025.
- Made final investment decision for the Hammerhead development in Guyana, anticipated online in 2029.

## Forward Signals

The filing does not provide specific quantitative guidance for 2026, but management expects Permian production to reach approximately 2.5 Moebd by 2030 and anticipates eight FPSO vessels in operation on the Stabroek Block by year-end 2030.

**Known trends**
- Management expects a shift in the geographic mix of Upstream production, with the proportion from the Americas generally increasing over the next several years.
- Refining margins are expected to remain volatile with changes in global factors, including geopolitical developments and demand growth.

| 2 | Geopolitical disruption: Transportation of Kazakhstan oil through the CPC pipeline could be disrupted, curtailed, or suspended, potentially causing a loss of cash flows of uncertain duration. | In the event geopolitical issues escalate in the region, including ongoing military conflict, it is possible that the transportation of Kazakhstan oil through the CPC pipeline could be disrupted, curtailed, temporarily suspended, or otherwise restricted. |
| 3 | Climate change and energy transition: Government actions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions could increase compliance costs, reduce demand for hydrocarbons, and lengthen project implementation times. | Depending on how policies are formulated and applied, such policies could negatively affect our investment returns, make our hydrocarbon-based products more expensive or less competitive, lengthen project implementation times, and reduce demand for hydrocarbons. |
| 4 | Cybersecurity: The company is regularly subject to attempted cybersecurity disruptions from state-sponsored actors, which could cause physical harm, damage assets, or compromise business systems. | ExxonMobil is regularly subject to attempted cybersecurity disruptions from a variety of sources including state-sponsored actors. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt (short-term notes and loans payable plus long-term debt) was $43.5B at year-end 2025, compared to $41.7B at year-end 2024. Cash and cash equivalents declined to $10.7B from $23.0B, resulting in a net debt position of $32.8B, up from $18.7B.

Liquidity: Cash and cash equivalents of $10.7B, supplemented by access to debt markets; the company issued $2.3B in long-term debt and $2.4B in short-term debt during 2025.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $52.0B, investing $-25.9B, financing $-39.1B.

Working capital: Current assets $83.4B vs. current liabilities $72.3B (current ratio 1.15x). A year earlier: $92.0B vs. $70.3B (1.31x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Long-term debt of $34.2B at year-end 2025, with $9.3B in notes and loans payable classified as current.

## The Print

Pfizer reported Q1 2026 net income of $2.69B ($0.47 diluted EPS) on revenue of $14.45B, a 5% YoY increase.

Revenue growth accelerated to 5% YoY (2% operational) while net income declined due to higher cost of sales and R&D expenses, partially offset by lower restructuring charges.

- Total revenues increased 5% YoY to $14.45B, driven by growth in Padcev, Eliquis, Oncology biosimilars, and Nurtec ODT/Vydura, partially offset by declines in COVID-19 products.
- Net income decreased 9% YoY to $2.69B, with diluted EPS of $0.47 compared to $0.52 in the prior-year quarter.
- Operating cash flow was $2.62B, up from $2.34B in Q1 2025, while free cash flow improved to $2.18B from $1.77B.

## Results That Matter

| Operating income | $3.17B | $2.79B | +13.6% | Increase primarily due to higher revenues and lower restructuring charges, partially offset by higher cost of sales and R&D expenses. |

| Diluted EPS | $0.47 | $0.52 | −9.6% | Decline reflects lower net income, partially offset by a slight increase in weighted-average diluted shares. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net income of $2.69B included $100M in restructuring charges and acquisition-related costs (down from $678M in Q1 2025), $137M in acquired IPR&D expenses, and a $295M unfavorable change in contingent consideration liabilities. Excluding these items, adjusted earnings would be higher, but the filing does not provide a non-GAAP reconciliation.

Operating cash flow was 1.0x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $2.2B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $2.4B (prior $2.4B); capital expenditures $436.0M (prior $564.0M).

Pfizer continued to return capital to shareholders through dividends ($2.45B paid) while reducing debt and investing in R&D and acquisitions. The company completed the exit of its ViiV investment for $1.875B in cash proceeds after quarter-end, strengthening liquidity.

Return on equity was 3.0%; return on assets 1.3%.

- Completed exit of 11.7% investment in ViiV on March 31, 2026, receiving $1.875 billion in cash proceeds.
- Acquired Metsera in November 2025 for $8.0 billion, expanding obesity and cardiometabolic pipeline.

## Forward Signals

The filing does not provide updated full-year 2026 guidance in this 10-Q. Management reiterates expectations for an unfavorable revenue impact from patent expiries of approximately $1.5 billion in 2026.

**Known trends**
- Patent-based or regulatory exclusivity expiries expected to significantly accelerate over the next few years, with an estimated $1.5 billion unfavorable revenue impact in 2026.
- U.S. government announced Section 232 tariffs on imported patented pharmaceuticals, up to 100% duty, set to phase in on July 31, 2026, subject to final negotiation of Pfizer's tariff agreement.

**Subsequent events**
- On March 31, 2026, Pfizer completed the exit of its ViiV investment, receiving $1.875 billion in cash proceeds.

In 2026, we continue to expect an unfavorable revenue impact from patent-based or regulatory exclusivity expiries of approximately $1.5 billion. |

These measures, featuring exemptions for commitments to onshore and invest in U.S. manufacturing, are set to phase in on July 31, 2026, and the application to Pfizer is subject to the final negotiation of our tariff agreement with the U.S. Government. |

Negotiated prices for Ibrance and Xtandi are expected to follow in 2027, with Xeljanz effective in 2028. |

Liquidity: Cash and equivalents of $1.7B plus short-term investments of $11.4B provide liquidity. Operating cash flow of $2.6B in Q1 2026 covers dividends and capital expenditures. The company also has access to credit facilities, though not detailed in this filing.

## The Print

Ford's Q1 2026 net income attributable to Ford rose to $2.548B ($0.63 diluted EPS) from $471M a year earlier, driven by higher Ford Blue and Ford Pro EBIT and a one-time IEEPA tariff benefit.

Net income and adjusted EBIT improved significantly year-over-year, but operating cash flow and free cash flow deteriorated due to working capital changes and higher capital spending.

- Revenue increased 6% YoY to $43.253B, with Ford Blue revenue up 14% and Ford Pro revenue down 3%.
- Company adjusted EBIT was $3.488B, up from $1.019B, with adjusted EBIT margin of 8.1%.
- Operating cash flow fell to $1.316B from $3.679B, and free cash flow was negative $1.060B.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $43.253B | $40.659B | +6.4% | Revenue increase driven by favorable mix, exchange, and net pricing in Ford Blue, partially offset by lower Ford Pro wholesales. |
| Operating income | $2.329B | $319M | +630.1% | Operating income increased primarily due to higher Ford Blue and Ford Pro EBIT and a one-time IEEPA tariff benefit. |
| Operating margin | 5.4% | 0.8% | +4.6 ppts | Operating margin improved due to higher revenue and operating income, with cost controls and favorable market factors. |
| Diluted EPS | $0.63 | $0.12 | +425.0% | Diluted EPS increased due to higher net income and a modest increase in diluted shares outstanding. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net income included $226 million of pre-tax special item charges, primarily restructuring in Europe and EV program cancellations, partially offset by pension and OPEB remeasurement gains. Excluding special items, adjusted EPS was $0.66 versus reported $0.63.

Operating cash flow was 0.5x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $-1.1B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $607.0M (prior $1.2B), share repurchases $311.0M; capital expenditures $2.4B (prior $1.8B).

Ford's capital allocation reflects a shift toward debt reduction and shareholder returns, with the repayment of the $2.3B convertible notes and initiation of share repurchases, while maintaining a target of 40-50% of adjusted free cash flow for distributions.

Return on equity was 6.8%; return on assets 0.9% (prior 0.2%).

- Settled $2.3B 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes in cash and issued 6.6 million shares from treasury to settle the conversion premium, subsequently repurchased under anti-dilutive program.
- Declared a regular dividend of $0.15 per share in Q1 2026, compared to $0.30 per share (including supplemental) in Q1 2025.

## Forward Signals

No specific full-year 2026 guidance provided in this filing, but management expects to partially recover production lost due to Novelis fires in the second half of 2026 and anticipates a tax benefit of up to $350 million from U.S. Qualified Opportunity Zone incentives in Q2 2026.

**Known trends**
- Trade policy and tariffs: expects about $2.8 billion in tariff reimbursements, with timing uncertain.
- EV market rationalization: cancelled three planned EVs and ending F-150 Lightning production; may incur up to $4 billion in additional charges.
- Aluminum supply disruption from Novelis fires: lower production in Q1, partial recovery expected in H2 2026.

**Subsequent events**
- Expected closing of BOSK joint venture disposition in Q2 2026, with pre-tax special item charges of about $3.5 billion.

## The Print

Ford's Q1 2026 net income attributable to Ford rose to $2.5B ($0.63 diluted EPS) from $471M a year earlier, driven by higher Ford Blue and Ford Pro EBIT and a one-time IEEPA tariff benefit.

Net income and adjusted EBIT increased sharply year-over-year, primarily due to higher Ford Blue and Ford Pro EBIT, a one-time IEEPA tariff benefit, and lower regulatory compliance expenses, partially offset by higher taxes and special item charges.

- Net income attributable to Ford increased to $2,548M from $471M in Q1 2025.
- Diluted EPS rose to $0.63 from $0.12 a year ago.
- Company adjusted EBIT was $3,488M, up from $1,019M in Q1 2025.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $43,253M | $40,659M | +6.4% | Revenue increased primarily due to favorable mix, exchange, and net pricing in Ford Blue, partially offset by lower Ford Pro wholesales. |
| Operating income | $2,329M | $319M | +630.1% | Operating income increased primarily due to higher Ford Blue and Ford Pro EBIT and a one-time IEEPA tariff benefit. |
| Operating margin | 5.4% | 0.8% | +4.6 ppts | Operating margin improved due to higher EBIT and revenue growth. |
| Diluted EPS | $0.63 | $0.12 | +425.0% | Diluted EPS increased due to higher net income, partially offset by a higher share count. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net income included $226M of pre-tax special item charges, primarily restructuring in Europe and EV program cancellations, partially offset by a $175M pension and OPEB remeasurement gain. Excluding special items, adjusted EPS was $0.66 versus reported $0.63.

Operating cash flow was 0.5x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $-1.1B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $607.0M (prior $1.2B), share repurchases $311.0M; capital expenditures $2.4B (prior $1.8B).

Ford continued to return capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases, while increasing capital spending on product development and electrification. The company settled its convertible notes in cash and repurchased shares under its anti-dilutive program.

Return on equity was 6.8%; return on assets 0.9% (prior 0.2%).

- Settled $2.3B 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes in cash and issued 6.6 million shares to settle the conversion premium, subsequently repurchased.
- Declared a regular dividend of $0.15 per share in Q1 2026, compared to a regular plus supplemental dividend of $0.30 per share in Q1 2025.

## Forward Signals

The filing does not provide explicit full-year guidance, but management expects to partially recover production lost due to the Novelis fires in the second half of 2026 and anticipates recognizing a tax benefit of up to $350M from U.S. Qualified Opportunity Zone tax incentives in Q2 2026.

**Known trends**
- Trade policy and tariffs: expects about $2.8B in tariff reimbursements, with timing uncertain.
- EV market rationalization: cancelled three planned EVs and ending F-150 Lightning production; may incur up to $4B in additional charges.
- Aluminum supply disruption from Novelis fires: lower production in Q1, partial recovery expected in H2 2026.

**Subsequent events**
- Expected closing of BOSK joint venture disposition in Q2 2026, with pre-tax special item charges of about $3.5B.

> "Although we have started to receive reimbursements from the federal government (excluding those related to IEEPA), the timing for our receipt of these reimbursements is uncertain and is subject to changes in trade policy." — Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Trade policy and tariffs could materially impact results; timing of reimbursements uncertain. | As of March 31, 2026, we expect to receive about $2.8 billion related to tariff reimbursements from the federal government and suppliers and offsets to Company payment obligations to suppliers. Included in this amount is about $1.3 billion related to the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (“IEEPA”) and tariff rulings from the United States Supreme Court and the Court of International Trade in the first quarter of 2026. |
| 2 | EV market rationalization may lead to substantial charges and adverse impact on results. | In December 2025, we announced our decision to rationalize our EV manufacturing capacity and product roadmap, including cancelling three previously planned EVs and ending production of the current generation F-150 Lightning EV. Related to the foregoing, in the first quarter of 2026, we recorded $103 million of charges to be paid in cash, primarily related to contractual commitments related to those programs. As previously disclosed, we may incur additional expenses and cash expenditures of up to about $4 billion (on a pre-tax basis) related to these actions and will recognize those charges in the quarter they are incurred as a special item. |
| 3 | Aluminum supply disruption from Novelis fires caused lower production; recovery expected in H2 2026. | As previously disclosed, in September 2025 and November 2025, fires at a Novelis Inc. plant in New York disrupted operations at the facility. Novelis is a major aluminum supplier to Ford, and since the initial fire occurred, we have been working closely with Novelis to address the situation and exploring potential alternative sources of aluminum. We have also sought mitigating actions to minimize potential disruptions to our operations. We experienced lower production subsequent to the Novelis fires in September and November 2025, and although the ultimate impact on Ford depends on a number of factors, in the second half of 2026, we expect to partially recover the production lost to date. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt (Company excluding Ford Credit) was $19.6B at March 31, 2026, down from $21.9B at December 31, 2025. Cash net of debt (excluding finance leases) was $3.3B, down from $7.7B.

Liquidity: Company cash was $22.0B and liquidity was $43.1B at March 31, 2026, down from $28.7B and $49.8B respectively at December 31, 2025. The decrease in cash reflects repayment of convertible notes and share repurchases.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $1.3B, investing $-771.0M, financing $-6.2B.

Working capital: Current assets $116.3B vs. current liabilities $106.7B (current ratio 1.09x). A year earlier: $123.5B vs. $114.9B (1.07x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Settled $2.3B 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes in cash on March 16, 2026.
- Ford Credit debt totaled $137.5B at March 31, 2026, with $47.5B payable within one year.

| Note 14 - Employee Separation Actions | Restructuring charges of $368M in Q1 2026, with total 2026 charges expected between $500M and $1B. |
| Note 16 - Variable Interest Entities: BOSK JVDA | Expected pre-tax special item charges of about $3.5B upon closing in Q2 2026. |

## The Print

Walmart's fiscal 2026 revenue reached $713.2B, up 4.7% YoY, with net income of $21.9B and diluted EPS of $2.73.

Revenue growth moderated slightly from 5.1% in fiscal 2025 to 4.7% in fiscal 2026, while net income growth accelerated due to a $2.1B net gain on investments (vs. a $0.8B loss in the prior year).

- Total revenue increased 4.7% to $713.2B, driven by comparable sales growth across all segments.
- Net income attributable to Walmart rose 12.6% to $21.9B, while diluted EPS increased 13.3% to $2.73.
- Operating cash flow grew 14.1% to $41.6B, funding increased capital expenditures of $26.6B and higher shareholder returns.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $713.2B | $681.0B | +4.7% | Increase driven by strong positive comparable sales across U.S. segments and international markets, with growth in average ticket, transactions, and unit volumes. |
| Operating income | $29.8B | $29.3B | +1.7% | Increase primarily due to higher gross profit, partially offset by higher operating expenses as a percentage of net sales. |
| Operating margin | 4.2% | 4.3% | −0.1 ppts | Decrease driven by higher self-insured general liability claims expense, a PhonePe share-based compensation charge, and increased depreciation. |
| Diluted EPS | $2.73 | $2.41 | +13.3% | Increase driven by higher net income and a lower share count due to share repurchases. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net income includes a $2.1B net gain on investments (vs. a $0.8B net loss in fiscal 2025), which is non-operating and volatile. Excluding this item, operating income grew only 1.6%, reflecting margin pressure from higher expenses.

Operating cash flow was 1.9x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $14.9B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $7.5B (prior $6.7B), share repurchases $8.1B (prior $4.5B); capital expenditures $26.6B (prior $23.8B).

Capital allocation remained focused on omnichannel growth, with capital expenditures increasing 12.0% to $26.6B, primarily for supply chain, technology, and store remodels. Shareholder returns accelerated, with dividends up 12.2% and share repurchases up 80.0%, funded by strong operating cash flow.

Return on equity was 22.0% (prior 21.4%); return on assets 7.7% (prior 7.5%).

- In February 2026, the Board approved a new $30.0B share repurchase authorization, replacing the remaining $4.0B under the prior program.
- Effective February 19, 2026, the annual dividend was increased to $0.99 per share, up from $0.94.

## Forward Signals

Management projects capital expenditures for fiscal 2027 to be approximately $25B to $27B, with a focus on technology, supply chain, and customer-facing initiatives.

**Known trends**
- Continued uncertainty due to tariffs and trade restrictions, inflationary trends, and currency fluctuations.
- Less than one third of U.S. merchandise is imported, with most imports from China, Mexico, Vietnam, India, and Canada.

**Subsequent events**
- In February 2026, the Board approved a new $30.0B share repurchase authorization.
- Effective February 19, 2026, the annual dividend was increased to $0.99 per share.

> "We expect continued uncertainty in our business and the global economy due to the following factors: tariffs and trade restrictions; inflationary trends; fluctuations in global currencies; swings in macroeconomic conditions and their effect on consumer confidence; changes in employment trends; volatility in fuel prices; and supply chain pressures, any of which may impact our results." — Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Failure to successfully execute the omnichannel strategy and the cost of investments in eCommerce and technology may adversely affect market position, net sales, and financial performance. | Failure to successfully execute our omnichannel strategy and the cost of our investments in eCommerce and technology may materially adversely affect our market position, net sales and financial performance. |
| 2 | Strong competition from other retailers, wholesale club operators, and omnichannel retailers could materially adversely affect financial performance. | We face strong competition from other retailers, wholesale club operators, omnichannel retailers and other businesses which could materially adversely affect our financial performance. |
| 3 | General or macro-economic factors, including higher interest rates, inflation, and changes in consumer spending, may materially adversely affect financial performance. | General or macro-economic factors, both domestically and internationally, may materially adversely affect our financial performance. |
| 4 | Any failure to maintain the privacy or security of information relating to customers, members, associates, and vendors could damage reputation and result in litigation, fines, and increased costs. | Any failure to maintain the privacy or security of the information relating to our company, customers, members, associates, business partners and vendors, whether as a result of cyberattacks on our information systems or otherwise, could damage our reputation, result in litigation or other legal actions against us, result in fines, penalties, and liability, cause us to incur substantial additional costs and materially adversely affect our business and operating results. |

## Segments

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Walmart U.S. | $485.6B | $25.2B | +4.4% | 68% of segment revenue, 5% operating margin |
| Walmart International | $132.0B | $5.1B | +7.0% | 19% of segment revenue, 4% operating margin — Net sales growth of 7.0% was driven by positive comparable sales across international markets, including strong eCommerce growth of $6.3B, partially offset by $2.8B of negative currency fluctuations. |
| Sam's Club U.S. | $95.5B | $2.4B | +3.2% | 13% of segment revenue, 3% operating margin |

## The Print

Walmart's fiscal 2026 revenue rose 4.7% to $713.2B, with net income of $21.9B and diluted EPS of $2.73.

- Total revenue increased 4.7% to $713.2B, driven by comparable sales growth across all segments.

- Diluted EPS increased 13.3% to $2.73, reflecting higher net income and share repurchases.

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $713.2B | $681.0B | +4.7% | Growth driven by positive comparable sales across U.S. segments and international markets, with strength in eCommerce and grocery. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net income includes a $2.1B net gain on investments (other gains and losses), which is non-operating and volatile. Excluding this gain, operating performance was solid but less robust. Additionally, operating expenses included a $0.9B self-insurance charge and a $0.7B PhonePe share-based compensation charge, which are unusual items.

Operating cash flow was 1.9x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $14.9B.

Capital returned — dividends paid $7.5B (prior $6.7B), share repurchases $8.1B (prior $4.5B); capital expenditures $26.6B (prior $23.8B).

## The Print

Boeing swung to a net profit of $2.2B in 2025 from a $11.8B loss in 2024, driven by a $9.6B gain on the Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture and higher commercial deliveries.

Boeing returned to profitability in 2025, driven by a $9.6B gain on the Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture, higher commercial aircraft deliveries, and lower defense program charges, partially offset by $5.3B in reach-forward losses on the 777X and 767 programs.

- Revenue increased 34.5% to $89.5B, with Commercial Airplanes revenue up 81.5% to $41.5B on higher deliveries.
- Net income attributable to Boeing shareholders was $2.2B, compared with a loss of $11.8B in 2024.
- Diluted EPS was $2.48, versus a loss of $18.36 per share in 2024.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $89.5B | $66.5B | +34.6% | Increase driven by higher deliveries at Commercial Airplanes, lower net unfavorable cumulative contract catch-up adjustments at Defense, Space & Security, and higher government and commercial services revenue at Global Services. |
| Operating income | $4.3B | -$10.7B | −59.8% | Increase driven by a $9.6B gain on the Digital Aviation Solutions Divestiture at Global Services, lower net unfavorable cumulative contract catch-up adjustments at Defense, Space & Security, and higher deliveries at Commercial Airplanes, partially offset by higher reach-forward losses on 777X and 767 programs. |
| Operating margin | 4.8% | -16.1% | +20.9 ppts | Margin improvement reflects the divestiture gain and lower defense program charges, partially offset by reach-forward losses on commercial programs. |
| Diluted EPS | $2.48 | -$18.36 | −86.5% | EPS improvement driven by the return to profitability, partially offset by mandatory convertible preferred stock dividends. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported operating income of $4.3B includes a $9.6B gain on the Digital Aviation Solutions Divestiture and $5.3B in reach-forward losses on the 777X and 767 programs. Excluding the divestiture gain, core operating earnings were $3.2B, still a significant improvement from the prior year's core operating loss of $11.8B.

Operating cash flow was 0.5x net income (cash conversion); free cash flow of $-1.9B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — dividends paid $331.0M; capital expenditures $2.9B (prior $2.2B).

Capital allocation in 2025 was dominated by the $8.4B Spirit AeroSystems acquisition (funded largely with stock and debt assumption) and the $10.6B Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture. Operating cash flow of $1.1B was insufficient to cover capital expenditures of $2.9B, resulting in negative free cash flow of $1.9B. The company paid $331M in mandatory convertible preferred stock dividends and did not repurchase common stock.

Return on equity was 41.0%; return on assets 1.3% (prior -7.6%).

- Completed acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems for total consideration of $8.4B, including $4.7B in Boeing common stock.
- Completed divestiture of portions of Digital Aviation Solutions business for $10.6B in cash, recognizing a $9.6B gain.

## Forward Signals

The filing does not provide specific quantitative guidance for 2026. Management discusses plans to increase 737 production rate to 47 per month in 2026 and expects first delivery of the 777-9 in 2027, but notes certification timing is determined by the FAA.

**Known trends**
- Global air traffic expanded near historical trend rates in 2025, with international demand outpacing domestic demand.
- Supply chain performance is improving but inflationary pressures and labor instability continue to challenge productivity.
- U.S. government funding uncertainty, including potential shutdowns, could impact defense and commercial operations.

**Subsequent events**
- On January 23, 2026, H.R. 6938 was enacted, funding certain federal departments including NASA through FY26.
- After January 30, 2026, the U.S. government will enter a partial shutdown unless full-year FY26 appropriations or an additional Continuing Resolution is enacted.

| 2 | Fixed-price development contracts at Defense, Space & Security have incurred significant losses, with $5.0B in additional losses on five major programs in 2024 and continued losses in 2025. | During 2024, BDS recorded $5.0 billion of additional losses on its five most significant fixed-price development programs (KC-46A Tanker, T-7A Red Hawk, Commercial Crew, VC-25B Presidential Aircraft, and MQ-25), which also affect cash flows in future periods. |

## The Print

Intel reported a Q1 2026 net loss of $3.7B ($0.73 diluted EPS) on revenue of $13.6B, driven by a $3.9B Mobileye goodwill impairment.

The quarter shifted from a modest operating loss to a substantial net loss due to a large non-cash goodwill impairment, despite revenue growth and improved gross margin.

- Revenue increased 7.2% YoY to $13.6B, led by a 22% increase in DCAI revenue.
- Net loss attributable to Intel widened to $3.7B from $821M a year earlier, primarily due to a $3.9B non-cash goodwill impairment charge related to Mobileye.
- Operating cash flow was $1.1B, up from $813M in Q1 2025, while free cash flow remained negative at -$2.5B.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $13.6B | $12.7B | +7.1% | Revenue growth was driven by higher Intel Products revenue, particularly a 22% increase in DCAI revenue from higher server ASPs. |
| Operating income | -$3.1B | -$301M | +929.9% | Operating loss widened primarily due to $3.9B in restructuring and other charges, including the Mobileye goodwill impairment. |
| Operating margin | -23.1% | -2.4% | −20.7 ppts | Margin decline was driven by the large restructuring and other charges, which were 30.0% of revenue in Q1 2026 versus 1.2% in Q1 2025. |
| Diluted EPS | -$0.73 | -$0.19 | +284.2% | EPS decline reflects the higher net loss attributable to Intel, driven by the goodwill impairment and higher interest and other net losses. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported operating loss of $3.1B includes $4.1B of restructuring and other charges, of which $3.9B is a non-cash goodwill impairment related to Mobileye. Excluding these charges, operating income would have been approximately $934M, compared to a loss of $145M in Q1 2025 (excluding $156M of charges). Additionally, interest and other net included a $1.1B loss from the mark-to-market of Escrowed Shares, partially offset by a $223M benefit from Ireland SCIP liquidated damages.

Operating cash flow was positive despite a net loss; free cash flow of $-2.5B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital expenditures $3.6B (prior $5.2B).

Capital expenditures of $3.6B exceeded operating cash flow of $1.1B, resulting in negative free cash flow of $2.5B. The company funded the shortfall with cash and investments, and continued to invest in manufacturing capacity and process technology. No dividends or share repurchases were made during the quarter.

Return on equity was -3.3%; return on assets -1.8%.

- In April 2026, Intel acquired Apollo's 49% minority interest in Ireland SCIP for approximately $14.2B, funded with cash, short-term investments, and a $6.5B term loan.
- Mobileye acquired Mentee Robotics for $637M in February 2026.

## Forward Signals

The filing does not provide specific quantitative guidance for future periods. Management expects supply constraints to persist throughout 2026 and anticipates total R&D and MG&A expenses to decrease in 2026 relative to recent historical periods.

**Known trends**
- Supply constraints from internal and external factors are expected to limit revenue growth throughout 2026.
- Industry-wide shortages of substrates, memory, and other critical components may further limit ability to meet customer demand.
- The company may pause or discontinue development of Intel 14A and successor nodes if sufficient committed demand is not secured.

**Subsequent events**
- On April 8, 2026, Intel completed the repurchase of Apollo's 49% minority interest in Ireland SCIP for approximately $14.2B.
- In April 2026, Intel executed and drew on a $6.5 billion 364-day senior unsecured term loan facility with an interest rate of 4.79%.

> "We expect these supply constraints to persist throughout 2026, and industry‑wide shortages of substrates, memory and other critical components may further limit our ability to fully meet customer demand." — Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Geopolitical risk from the Iran conflict could disrupt Intel's fabrication facility in Israel, which produces a significant portion of revenue on Intel 7. | A significant portion of our revenues are generated from products on Intel 7 manufactured at our fabrication facility in Israel. As we are not insured for business interruptions resulting from war or political violence, a disruption of that facility could have a significant adverse impact on our business. |
| 2 | Goodwill impairment risk: Mobileye reporting unit has $4.3B of remaining goodwill, and a 1% increase in discount rate would have caused an additional $682M impairment. | Should our estimates change based on Mobileye's operating results, market conditions, long-term growth projections, or other assumptions underlying our forecast, including changes in the discount rate, the Mobileye reporting unit may become subject to further impairment in future periods. |
| 3 | Legal contingencies: VLSI litigation accrual of $1.0B and EC fine accrual of $310M, with potential for additional losses. | As of March 28, 2026, we have accrued liabilities of $1.0 billion related to litigation involving VLSI and $310 million, including revaluation effects and accrued interest, related to an EC-imposed fine. |

## Segments

| Segment | Revenue | Operating Income | Change | Commentary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Intel Products | $12.8B | $4.1B | +8.7% | 49% of segment revenue, 32% operating margin — Revenue increased 9% YoY, driven by DCAI's 22% growth from higher server ASPs; CCG revenue was modestly higher. Operating income improved due to lower operating expenses from restructuring and higher product profit in DCAI. |
| Client Computing | $7.7B | $2.5B | +1.3% | 30% of segment revenue, 33% operating margin — CCG revenue increased $98M, with client revenue up $54M driven by a 16% increase in ASPs, partially offset by a 13% volume decline due to supply constraints. |
| Datacenter and AI | $5.1B | $1.5B | +22.4% | 19% of segment revenue, 31% operating margin — DCAI revenue increased $926M, primarily from $696M higher server revenue on a 27% ASP increase, partially offset by a 5% volume decline. Operating income benefited from higher product profit and lower period charges. |
| Other | $628.0M | $102.0M | -33.4% | 2% of segment revenue, 16% operating margin — All other revenue decreased $315M due to Altera deconsolidation, partially offset by higher Mobileye revenue ($558M, up $120M). Operating income was roughly flat. |
| Intel Foundry |  | $-2.4B |  | Revenue increased $754M, driven by higher intersegment wafer volumes on Intel 18A, Intel 3, and Intel 4 nodes. Operating loss widened slightly due to higher costs on Intel 18A, partially offset by lower period charges. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total debt was $45.0B, with cash and short-term investments of $32.8B, resulting in net debt of $12.2B. Debt-to-equity was 0.40x.

Liquidity: Cash and cash equivalents of $17.2B plus short-term investments of $15.5B provide ample near-term liquidity. The company also has access to a $7.0B revolving credit facility and a $3.0B credit facility, with no borrowings outstanding.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $1.1B, investing $3.1B, financing $-1.2B.

Working capital: Current assets $62.2B vs. current liabilities $26.9B (current ratio 2.31x). A year earlier: $63.7B vs. $31.6B (2.02x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- In Q1 2026, Intel settled $1.5B of senior notes due February 2026.
- In April 2026, Intel drew on a $6.5B 364-day term loan facility to fund the Ireland SCIP repurchase.

## The Print

Rivian's 2025 revenue rose 8.4% to $5.39B while net loss narrowed to $3.65B, as the company achieved positive gross margin for the first time.

Rivian achieved positive gross profit for the first time, driven by higher average selling prices, cost reductions, and a significant increase in high-margin software and services revenue from the Volkswagen joint venture.

- Revenue increased 8.4% YoY to $5.39B, driven by a 222% surge in Software and Services revenue to $1.56B, partially offsetting a 14.6% decline in Automotive revenue.
- Net loss attributable to common stockholders narrowed 23.2% to $3.65B, with diluted loss per share improving to -$3.07 from -$4.69.
- Gross profit swung to positive $144M from a loss of $1.20B, as gross margin improved to 2.7% from -24.1%.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $5.39B | $4.97B | +8.4% | Total revenues increased primarily due to a 222% increase in Software and Services revenue, driven by vehicle electrical architecture and software development services for Volkswagen Group, partially offset by a 14.6% decline in Automotive revenue from lower deliveries. |
| Operating income | -$3.59B | -$4.69B | −23.4% | Operating loss narrowed primarily due to the improvement in gross profit, partially offset by higher SG&A expenses. |
| Operating margin | -66.5% | -94.3% | +27.8 ppts | Operating margin improved as revenue growth and cost reductions outpaced the increase in operating expenses. |
| Diluted EPS | -$3.07 | -$4.69 | −34.5% | Diluted loss per share improved due to the narrower net loss and a higher weighted-average share count from the Volkswagen investment and stock-based compensation. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net loss includes a $186M expense for securities class action litigation settlement (net of expected insurance recoveries), partially offset by a $101M gain on the equity method investment in Also, Inc. Excluding these items, the operating loss would have been approximately $3.48B, still reflecting underlying improvement from cost reductions and higher-margin software revenue.

Free cash flow of $-2.5B.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital expenditures $1.7B (prior $1.1B).

Capital allocation remained focused on scaling production capacity, with capital expenditures increasing 49.9% to $1.71B, primarily for the Normal Factory expansion to support R2 production. The company issued $750M of equity to Volkswagen Group and refinanced its 2026 Notes with 2031 Green Secured Notes, extending debt maturity while maintaining a high cash balance of $3.58B.

- Issued $750M of Class A common stock to Volkswagen Group upon achievement of the Financial Milestone.
- Issued $1.25B of 2031 Green Secured Notes to redeem the 2026 Notes, extending maturity to 2031.
- Entered into a DOE loan facility for up to $6.0B to fund the Stanton Springs North Facility.

## Forward Signals

Management expects customer deliveries of the R2 to begin in the second quarter of 2026 and anticipates continued improvement in automotive gross profit losses over time through the expected margin profile of R2, continued material cost improvements, and increased efficiencies. However, they also expect short-term higher conversion costs, lower overhead absorption, and increased warranty expenses as they ramp R2 production.

**Known trends**
- The expiration of 45W tax credits after September 30, 2025 negatively impacted vehicle deliveries and may continue to affect demand.
- Tariffs on imported automobile parts and materials could increase cost of revenues, though the company has obtained tariff offset credits through April 2030.
- The Joint Venture's combined performance obligation is expected to be satisfied by 2028, which may reduce software and services revenue thereafter.

## The Print

Coinbase reported a net loss of $394.1M on revenue of $1.41B for Q1 2026, with revenue down 30.5% YoY and diluted EPS of -$1.49.

Revenue declined sharply due to lower trading volume and crypto asset prices, while operating expenses rose, swinging the company to a net loss.

- Total revenue fell 30.5% YoY to $1.41B, driven by a 40% decline in transaction revenue to $755.8M.
- Net loss of $394.1M compared to net income of $65.6M in the prior-year quarter, with diluted EPS of -$1.49 vs. $0.24.
- Adjusted EBITDA was $303.3M, down 67% from $929.9M a year earlier.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $1,412,982,000 | $2,034,295,000 | −30.5% | Revenue decreased primarily due to a 40% decline in transaction revenue, driven by lower consumer and institutional trading volume. |
| Operating income | $-21,421,000 | $705,806,000 | −103.0% | Operating income turned negative as total operating expenses increased 8% while revenue fell 30.5%. |
| Operating margin | -1.5% | 34.7% | −36.2 ppts | Operating margin contracted sharply due to the revenue decline and higher technology and development expenses. |
| Diluted EPS | -$1.49 | $0.24 | +520.8% | Diluted EPS turned negative due to the net loss, with weighted-average diluted shares increasing to 264.8M from 271.3M. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net loss of $394.1M includes significant non-cash items: $482.4M in losses on crypto assets held for investment, $248.1M in stock-based compensation, and $68.0M in depreciation and amortization. Excluding these and other adjustments, Adjusted EBITDA was $303.3M, indicating positive core operating cash generation despite the GAAP loss.

Operating cash flow was positive despite a net loss.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital returned — share repurchases $1.1B.

The company repurchased $1.06B of Class A common stock during the quarter, utilizing a significant portion of its $4.0B repurchase authorization. This buyback was funded from existing cash reserves, which remain substantial at $10.2B. The allocation reflects management's confidence in long-term value despite current market softness.

Return on equity was -2.9% (prior 0.6%); return on assets -1.4%.

- Board increased share repurchase authorization from $2.0B to $4.0B in January 2026.
- No long-term debt has been repurchased under the program as of March 31, 2026.

## Forward Signals

Management provided qualitative guidance for Q2 2026: technology and development plus general and administrative expenses are expected to be generally lower than Q1 2026, and sales and marketing expenses are expected to be roughly in line with or lower than Q1 2026, reflecting the Restructuring Plan announced May 5, 2026.

**Known trends**
- Stablecoin adoption is accelerating, with USDC reaching an all-time high in market capitalization and average USDC held in Coinbase products.
- Trading volume decreased 50% YoY, driven by softer market conditions and a 44% decline in global crypto market spot trading volume.

**Subsequent events**
- On May 5, 2026, the company announced a Restructuring Plan to better align operating expenses with current market conditions and optimize operations for the AI era.

> "We announced the Everything Exchange in December 2025, and during the first quarter of 2026, we saw strong growth across derivatives, prediction markets, and decentralized exchange trading." — Management

## Risks

| # | Risk | Supporting Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Revenue concentration risk: one counterparty accounted for 23% of total revenue in Q1 2026, up from 15% in Q1 2025. | During the three months ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, one counterparty accounted for 23% and 15%, respectively, of total revenue. |
| 2 | Crypto asset price volatility directly impacts revenue and profitability, as evidenced by the $482.4M loss on crypto assets held for investment this quarter. | Losses on crypto assets held for investment, net decreased for the three months ended March 31, 2026 as compared to 2025, primarily due to fair value remeasurement. |
| 3 | Regulatory capital requirements: the company must maintain minimum net capital at subsidiaries, with CB Inc. required to hold $1,031M and CCTC $207M as of March 31, 2026. | As of March 31, 2026, we were in compliance with these capital requirements. |

## Balance Sheet & Liquidity

Leverage: Total long-term debt (including current portion) was $7.21B as of March 31, 2026, against cash and cash equivalents of $10.21B and shareholders' equity of $13.48B. Net cash position (cash minus total debt) was approximately $3.0B.

Liquidity: Cash and cash equivalents totaled $10.21B, with an additional $5.43B in customer custodial cash. Management believes existing cash, cash equivalents, and marketable investments of $10.4B are sufficient for short- and long-term requirements.

Cash flow: Cash flow — operating $182.7M, investing $-239.1M, financing $-864.9M.

Working capital: Current assets $19.7B vs. current liabilities $9.2B (current ratio 2.14x). A year earlier: $20.4B vs. $8.7B (2.34x).

**Maturities & covenants**
- Long-term debt includes $1.3B due within the next 12 months, classified as current liability; management intends to repay with cash at or prior to maturity.
- As of March 31, 2026, the company was in compliance with all regulatory capital requirements.

## The Print

Beyond Meat narrowed its net loss to $28.5M (diluted EPS -$0.06) on revenue of $58.2M, down 15.3% YoY, while gross margin turned positive at 3.4%.

The company achieved positive gross profit and significantly reduced operating losses, but revenue continued to decline due to weak category demand and distribution losses.

- Net loss improved to $28.5M from $61.1M in the prior-year quarter, driven by a $8.9M swing to positive gross profit and a $12.6M other income gain.
- Revenue declined 15.3% YoY to $58.2M, reflecting a 19.5% drop in volume, partially offset by a 5.4% increase in net revenue per pound.
- Gross margin turned positive at 3.4% versus -10.1% a year ago, helped by lower inventory provisions and reduced manufacturing costs.

## Results That Matter

| Metric | Current Period | Prior Period | Change | Investor Takeaway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Revenue | $58.2M | $68.7M | −15.3% | Decrease driven by a 19.5% decline in volume of products sold, partially offset by a 5.4% increase in net revenue per pound. |
| Operating income | -$41.1M | -$64.4M | −36.2% | Loss from operations narrowed due to higher gross profit and lower operating expenses. |
| Operating margin | -70.6% | -93.7% | +23.1 ppts | Margin improvement reflects cost reductions and positive gross margin. |
| Diluted EPS | -$0.06 | -$0.80 | −92.5% | EPS improvement driven by lower net loss and higher share count from conversions. |

## Earnings Quality & Cash Conversion

Reported net loss of $28.5M includes $11.9M non-cash gain from remeasurement of derivative liability, $6.1M gain on debt extinguishment, and $1.3M gain from warrant liability remeasurement. Excluding these one-time items, operating loss was $41.1M, and adjusted EBITDA was -$27.8M.

Free cash flow of $-7.6M.

## Value Drivers & Capital Allocation

Capital expenditures $2.5M (prior $4.5M).

Capital expenditures of $2.5M were focused on production equipment and facilities, funded by existing cash. The company continues to prioritize cost reduction and inventory management over expansion.

Return on assets -4.9%.

## Forward Signals

No specific financial guidance provided. Management expects to continue operating at a loss for the foreseeable future and may seek additional capital.

**Known trends**
- Persistent weak demand in the plant-based meat category, particularly refrigerated subsegment.
- Strategic repositioning to 'Beyond The Plant Protein Company' with expansion into beverages like Beyond Immerse.

**Subsequent events**
- Additional $62.6M principal amount of 2030 Notes converted into common stock after quarter end.
- Entered into a 10-year distribution agreement with Big Geyser for Beyond Immerse beverage line.

## Risks

| --- | --- | --- |

| 2 | Liquidity risk: company has a history of losses and negative operating cash flow; may need to raise additional capital, which could be dilutive. | We have a history of losses and negative cash flows from operating activities. We expect that we will continue to operate at a loss for the foreseeable future. |
| 3 | Debt covenant compliance: company was in default under Loan and Security Agreement for late delivery of audited financial statements, but remedied upon filing 10-K. | Because we failed to timely deliver to the lender by March 31, 2026 certain audited annual financial statements for our fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, as required by the terms of the Loan and Security Agreement, we were in default and provided notice thereof to the lender as required.
